tests.name: Soil texture (jar test)
tests.question: After mixing soil with water in a clear jar and letting it settle, which layer appears largest?

options.label: Mostly sand
options.interpretation: Coarse-textured soil; water may drain quickly and nutrient retention may be lower.

options.label: Mostly silt
options.interpretation: Medium-textured soil; confirm drainage and water-holding conditions.

options.label: Mostly clay
options.interpretation: Fine-textured soil; infiltration may be slower and compaction risk may be higher.

options.label: Layers look fairly balanced
options.interpretation: Possibly loam or mixed texture; laboratory texture testing is more reliable.

options.label: I don't know
options.interpretation: No texture-based adjustment should be made.

tests.name: Carbonate screening (vinegar test)
tests.question: When vinegar is added to a small dry soil sample, what happens?

options.label: Strong fizzing
options.interpretation: Possible carbonates; this does not establish soil pH.

options.label: Slight fizzing
options.interpretation: Possible low carbonate content; laboratory confirmation is needed.

options.label: No visible fizzing
options.interpretation: No obvious carbonate reaction; carbonates may still be present.

options.label: I don't know
options.interpretation: Do not infer carbonate status.

tests.name: Water drainage
tests.question: After water is poured into a small test hole in moist soil, how does it drain?

options.label: Drains quickly
options.interpretation: Possible rapid drainage and lower water retention.

options.label: Drains gradually
options.interpretation: Possible moderate drainage.

options.label: Water remains for a long time
options.interpretation: Possible poor drainage; investigate compaction or a high water table.

options.label: I don't know
options.interpretation: Do not make a drainage-based adjustment.

tests.name: Earthworm observation
tests.question: When examining a small area of moist soil, how many earthworms do you observe?

options.label: Several earthworms
options.interpretation: Earthworms are present; this can indicate biological activity but is not a complete soil-health measure.

options.label: One or two earthworms
options.interpretation: Some biological activity is present; results vary with season and moisture.

options.label: None observed
options.interpretation: No earthworms were observed; this alone does not prove poor soil health.

options.label: I don't know
options.interpretation: Do not infer biological activity.

tests.name: Soil pH
tests.question: What pH range does your soil test strip indicate?

options.label: Below 6.0
options.interpretation: Acidic soil; some crops may face nutrient availability limitations.
Slightly acidic soil; suitability depends on the crop.
Near-neutral soil; generally suitable for many crops.

options.label: Above 7.3
options.interpretation: Alkaline soil; some nutrients may become less available.

options.label: I don't know
options.interpretation: Do not make a pH-based adjustment.
